# Vendored: dyad-sh/dyad at 00d5f5af7fd0 (v1.15.0-beta.1, 2026-09-10)

Taken with `git archive` from the pinned commit: src, scaffold, worker, shared, packages, index.html,
package.json, package-lock.json, vite.renderer.config.mts, tsconfig*.json, components.json, LICENSE,
NOTICE, README.md, AGENTS.md.

Removed: `src/pro/` (Functional Source License 1.1; not reused). Everything kept is Apache 2.0 per
LICENSE.

Changes to reused files are listed here, one line each, so upstream can be tracked:

- `hologram.contracts.ts` (ours) also publishes imported input schemas as `window.__inputContracts`; the browser host validates and copies command inputs before effects, and returns typed refusals rather than synthesizing successful output.

- `src/pro/` is not Dyad's: four small files of ours export the names the renderer imports from the
  removed folder, so the renderer builds without the Functional Source License code:
  `shared/search_replace_parser.ts` (a parser for the SEARCH / REPLACE blocks the chat renders),
  `ui/components/Annotator/Annotator.tsx` (hands the screenshot back as one attachment; no drawing),
  `main/ipc/handlers/local_agent/tool_definitions.ts` (the tool name type; the names are the PrismPM tool contract's),
  `main/prompts/turbo_edits_v2_prompt.ts` (empty; turbo edits are a Pro feature and not offered).
- `scaffold/src/App.tsx`, as staged for the shell only (the vendored file is untouched): `<BrowserRouter basename={import.meta.env.BASE_URL}>`, so a project routes correctly when served under its address path instead of an origin root.
- `src/router.ts`: `basepath: import.meta.env.BASE_URL.replace(/\/$/, "")` on `createRouter`, so Dyad's routes live under the base the shell is served from (`/app/` locally, `/dyad-prism/app/` on Pages) and a refresh finds them.
- `src/components/preview_panel/PublishPanel.tsx`: one import and one mount of `HologramSection` (ours, `src/components/preview_panel/HologramSection.tsx`) above Dyad's deployment section, so the Publish panel offers "Publish as a Hologram application": the host composes a `.holo` v4 through PrismPM's own archive code in the core and serves it under its address. The words are the View's. For an app with rules the button says "publish" in the app's chat instead (through `useStreamChat`, as Dyad's Refactor button does), and the host builds the app with the Prism SDK on GitHub Actions (`shell/host.js` publishTurn).
- App covers (FA-28, `verification/app-covers.md`): `src/components/AppShowcaseCard.tsx` and `src/hooks/useAppThumbnails.ts` are replaced at build by ours (`hologram.screens/AppShowcaseCard.tsx`, `hologram.screens/useAppThumbnails.ts`, listed in `hologram.screens.mjs` SCREENS). The hook reads the cover, sentence and tag the browser host captured and checked (`shell/covers.mjs`) from the page's `covers` cache instead of asking the host for screenshot files; the card shows the cover at 2:1, then the name, the tag and the sentence held to two rows. Two patches widen the home's featured row to fit it (`src/components/FeaturedAppShowcase.tsx`: `w-56` becomes `w-72`, the See more tile `aspect-[4/3]` becomes `aspect-[2/1]`). `hologram.env.d.ts` declares `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`, which Vite replaces at build.
- `vite.shell.config.mts` (ours, added): the vendored Vite config plus fixed output names, so the shell's projected homepage can reference `assets/index.js` and `assets/index.css`; the renderer is now the homepage at the shell's root, the `--base` is the shell's base.
- The product's name: `vite.shell.config.mts` replaces every standalone `Dyad` word in `src/**` (sources, locales, markdown) with `Hologram` at build time and resolves `assets/logo.svg` to Hologram's mark; identifiers (`DyadError`, `dyad-write`, `__dyadIpcEnvelope`) are untouched. The vendored files themselves keep Dyad's words. `scripts/stamp_shell.py` does the same for the staged scaffold (the badge reads "Made with Hologram" and links to gethologram.ai).
- Three controls removed at build (`vite.shell.config.mts`): the setup pill under the home composer ("Manage AI setup" / "Connect AI to build", `src/pages/home.tsx`, its condition becomes `false`), the Pro selector (`src/components/ChatInputControls.tsx`, `<ProModeSelector />` becomes `{null}`); and the voice to text button (Dyad's Pro feature) is hidden by `shell/appearance.css` through its labels. The vendored files are untouched.
- `src/components/ModelPicker.tsx` is replaced at build by ours (`vendor/dyad/hologram.ModelPicker.tsx`, aliased in `vite.shell.config.mts`): two models, GLM 5.3 Flash (Cloud) and BitNet 2B (Local), each tagged with where it runs. Dyad's picker carries an "All models" submenu, a recent section, per model effort levels, price badges, a trial banner, local provider submenus for Ollama and LM Studio, and an "Unlock all models with Pro" row; none of those apply here. Ours writes what Dyad's wrote, the settings record's `selectedModel` and the chat's own selection once the chat has a history, so every screen stays in sync.
- `src/components/ChatInputControls.tsx`: the chat mode selector is removed at build (`<ChatModeSelector />` becomes `{null}`) and the host keeps the record's mode on build. This host implements one mode, Dyad's text tag build turn; its agent and plan modes promise tool calls that are not made here, and the composer showed "Basic Agent" while a build turn ran.
- `src/components/chat/ChatInput.tsx`: the promo row under the composer is not rendered (`{showPromo && <PromoMessage seed={promo.seed} />}` becomes `{null}`). Its messages sell Dyad Pro and point at Dyad's GitHub, subreddit and X account; the word transform would put Hologram's name on all of it.
- `src/renderer.tsx`: one import is prepended at build, `vendor/dyad/hologram.contracts.ts` (ours), which publishes every contract's output schema on the page as `window.__contracts`. Dyad's renderer types its calls but validates nothing it receives, so a host answer of the wrong shape used to reach a screen and crash it far from the cause; `shell/host.js` now parses every answer against the channel's own contract.
- The ui components are shadcn/ui new-york-v4 as the Hologram brand kit vendors it, not Dyad's (`hologram.ui.mjs`, ours, used by `vite.shell.config.mts`): every import of a name the kit has (`@/components/ui/button`, or a relative `./ui/button`) resolves to the kit's file under `vendor/shadcn-ui/registry/new-york-v4/` (written by `tools/live_components.mjs --vendor`, digests in `vendor/shadcn-ui/VENDORED.sha256`), and the build refuses a bundle that holds Base UI or Dyad's copy of a kit component. Dyad's own `src/components/ui/*` are untouched and never shipped; its five components the kit does not have (`ColorPicker`, `LoadingBar`, `NumberInput`, `SimpleAvatar`, `back-button`) are kept and are built from the kit's. Tailwind scans the kit's directory (`@source`, added to `globals.css` at build).
- Every screen's calls to those components are rewritten at build from Base UI's props to Radix's (`hologram.radix.mjs`, ours): `render={<El/>}` and `as` become `asChild`, Accordion and ToggleGroup take `type`, `TooltipProvider delay` is `delayDuration`, `closeOnClick={false}` is `onSelect` preventing default, `keepMounted` is `forceMount`, a `SelectValue` render function is called with its Select's value, `MiniSelectTrigger` is the kit's `SelectTrigger` at `size="sm"`, a `CommandDialog` filter goes on a cmdk `Command` inside it, a relative ui import names `@/components/ui/`. The vendored files are untouched. `hologram.typecheck.mjs` (ours, with `tsconfig.hologram.json` and `tsconfig.hologram.dyad.json`) typechecks the rewritten screens against the kit's components and refuses an error Dyad's own sources do not have, or a call the rewrite could not convert.
- The shell's own screens, after shadcn's dashboard-01 block and built only from the kit's components, through `hologram.screens.mjs` (ours, applied by `vite.shell.config.mts` and by the typecheck): `src/components/app-sidebar.tsx` is replaced whole by `hologram.screens/AppSidebar.tsx` (an inset sidebar that collapses to icons: Prism's mark, a triangle of three faces drawn in the text colour, and the name "Prism AI Foundry" (collapsed to icons, the mark alone, centred over the icons), New app, Home, Apps, Templates, Library, Plugins, the user's apps with the open app's chats, Settings and Help, plus the site header), and `src/pages/apps.tsx` by `hologram.screens/AppsPage.tsx` (section cards with trend badges from the apps' and chats' own dates, tabs with counts, a data table with row selection, a row menu and Dyad's bulk delete, and Dyad's collection views and dialogs). `src/components/ui/back-button.tsx` is replaced by `hologram.screens/BackButton.tsx`, which draws nothing: the site header carries a breadcrumb (the kit's Breadcrumb) to the page above. Each is compiled at the path of the file it replaces. Patches, each refusing the build if its passage is gone (a retag patch renames one element and its closing tag, found by the TypeScript parser): `src/pages/settings.tsx` draws each settings section as the kit's Card and drops its own title (the header names the page); `src/pages/plugins.tsx`, `src/pages/templates.tsx` and `src/pages/library-home.tsx` take the inset's page spacing and keep their description and actions without a second title; `src/pages/app-details.tsx` sits on the kit's Card instead of a box styled as one, and shows its dates as dates; `src/app/layout.tsx` puts the page in the sidebar's `SidebarInset` under the site header and opens the sidebar by default; `src/components/ZoomSelector.tsx` names the chosen level's label alone in the trigger (Radix shows the chosen item whole, description included). `hologram.env.d.ts` (ours) types an imported `.svg` for the typecheck.
- `src/pages/chat.tsx`, through `hologram.screens.mjs`: on a phone (the kit's `useIsMobile`, the sidebar's own 768 px breakpoint) the build screen returns `hologram.screens/MobileBuild.tsx` (ours, kit components only) instead of the two resizable panels: one pane at a time (chat, or the preview panel in its preview or publish mode, both kept mounted) and a bottom bar with back to the apps and Chat / Preview / Publish as the kit's `Tabs`. Two patches: one import line, and `const isMobile = useIsMobile(); if (isMobile) return <MobileBuild ... />;` before the `PanelGroup`. Wider screens are unchanged.
- The composer's + menu (`src/components/chat/AuxiliaryActionsMenu.tsx`), through `hologram.screens.mjs`: its Attach files and Themes submenus open in the kit's `DropdownMenuPortal`, and scroll within the screen when long. Inside the menu, which scrolls and is transformed while it animates in, they were clipped to its box, so their items could not be seen. The menu opens from the + at the composer's left (`align="start"`, 8 px from the screen's edge). A `showImport` prop adds "Import app" to the menu, opening the shell's `ImportAppDialog`. `src/components/chat/HomeChatInput.tsx` passes it, and `src/pages/home.tsx` drops its Import App button and that button's import, so Home's one entry point is the composer. The build screen's composer has no Import app item.
- `package.json`, `package-lock.json`: `radix-ui` 1.6.7 added, exactly as the brand kit's showcase pins it (the kit's components import it); npm moved the `@radix-ui/*` packages Dyad already had through `cmdk` and `vaul` to the versions it requires, and `react-remove-scroll` from 2.7.1 to 2.7.2.
- `hologram.GitHubIntegration.tsx` (ours) replaces `src/components/GitHubIntegration.tsx` at build time through `resolveId` in `vite.shell.config.mts`: Settings → Integrations → GitHub takes a pasted token (checked once against api.github.com), because GitHub's device flow is not served to web pages. Publishing uses it to build apps with the Prism SDK.
- The first load is lean (`hologram.lean.mjs`, ours, merged into `hologram.screens.mjs`'s patches so the build and the typecheck apply them, each refusing the build when its passage is gone): every route but home is a chunk of its own through TanStack's `lazyRouteComponent` (`src/routes/*.ts{,x}`), and `src/router.ts` preloads a route on intent (`defaultPreload: "intent"`) and names what it is loading when a chunk is slow; `src/components/preview_panel/PreviewPanel.tsx` loads its Code, Configure, Publish, Security, Tests, Plan and Problems panels with `React.lazy`, each behind a "Loading …" state drawn with the kit's Skeleton; `src/components/chat/CodeHighlight.tsx` hands shiki its eighteen grammars as dynamic imports, made when the first block is highlighted; `src/i18n/index.ts` keeps English in the first load and fetches another language when it is chosen, before the switch; `src/components/chat/monaco.ts` defines its themes on the first `loader.init()` an editor asks for, where it used to call it at import, which fetched Monaco (some 750 KB from cdn.jsdelivr.net) on every page load. `src/pages/chat.tsx`'s panels no longer animate their width. The measurements are in `studio/PERFORMANCE.md`.
- `posthog-js` and `posthog-js/react` resolve to `hologram.posthog.ts` (ours, `vite.shell.config.mts`): a client that sends nothing. Dyad's `posthog.init` reached Dyad's own PostHog project (`us.i.posthog.com`, three requests) on every load, with the visitor's address, even with telemetry off; this product sends nothing there. Settings still shows Dyad's Telemetry switch, which now changes nothing.
- Patches now apply to `.ts` modules as well as `.tsx` (`vite.shell.config.mts`, `hologram.typecheck.mjs`), and both refuse a build in which any patch was never applied (`unapplied()` in `hologram.screens.mjs`): a patch to a `.ts` file used to be skipped without a word.
- Chunks other than the entry are named by content (`assets/[name]-[hash].js`); `assets/index.js` and `assets/index.css` keep their fixed names, which the projected page references. The build writes `dist/.vite/manifest.json` for the Performance gate; it is not copied into the shell.
- `hologram.screens/AppsPage.tsx`: under the container's `@xl` width the four figures sit two by two without their footnotes, so the list starts on the first screen of a phone.
- `src/app/layout.tsx`: the first prompt's settle delay is 0 (`hologram.lean.mjs`), as Dyad's own test mode runs it; it held Home on screen for 2,000 ms after the stream had started. `src/pages/home.tsx`: the page fetches the chat page's chunk when idle, so Enter finds it ready, and the idea chips are the kit's outline Button (retag patches) instead of hand-styled buttons.
- `hologram.screens/AppSidebar.tsx`: on a phone a choice in the sidebar's Sheet closes it, and its items carry no tooltip (the kit opened one unseen on focus, so the first Escape closed that and not the Sheet).
- `hologram.ImportAppDialog.tsx` (ours) replaces `src/components/ImportAppDialog.tsx` at build time through `resolveId` in `vite.shell.config.mts` (its one user is `ImportAppButton.tsx`; `AI_RULES_PROMPT` is still exported): Import App on the home page takes a Forge export file (`hologram-forge/export/1`, written by the moved page of the site Forge was served from before) and the host's `forge:import` writes its apps, chats, files and versions under new ids. Dyad's dialog imports a folder from disk or a GitHub repository, neither of which a web page has. The file never carries settings or keys.
- Two decisions on the renderer's screens are the Forge kernel's (FK-16, FK-17 and FK-21, `app/src`), asked through `window.__forgeKernel` (`shell/host.js`): `src/pages/chat.tsx` shows upstream's MobileBuild (one pane at a time and a bar at the bottom) when the kernel answers `tabs` for the window's width, instead of the kit's `useIsMobile`, keeping the last answer for the next visit (`useNarrow`, `hologram.lean.mjs`); `hologram.screens/AppsPage.tsx` counts as this week what the kernel answers `yes` for, and shows a dash until every answer is in.
- `src/pages/home.tsx`, through `hologram.screens.mjs`: the suggestion chips' row gains `data-slot="home-suggestions"`, so `shell/appearance.css` can give the chips frosted glass that reads over Immersive's photo.
- `src/renderer.tsx` and `src/user_input/read_model.ts` (`hologram.lean.mjs`): a background query or the start-up hydration that meets a capability the browser host does not have (the typed `unsupportedChannel` refusal, FA-15) shows no toast; the screen draws its own empty state. Home greeted every visitor with four red errors (prompts, themes, custom themes, pending user input). An action the visitor takes still says the capability is unavailable.
- `src/errors/dyad_error.ts` (`hologram.lean.mjs`): a typed error reads as its message. Its class name `DyadError` is the protocol identifier the host and renderer share, so it stays; but `error.toString()` and every message built with `${error}` printed it, and visitors saw toasts that began "DyadError:".
- Home on a phone, through `hologram.screens.mjs` and `hologram.screens/AppSidebar.tsx`, styled by `shell/appearance.css` with every measure from the golden ratio: `src/pages/home.tsx` names its page and stage (`data-slot="home-page"`, `"home-stage"`), gives the headline and its words a short phone form ("Build anything", "Describe it. Dyad makes it real.") beside the wide one, adds a "Surprise me" button (the kit's Button) that writes a random idea into the composer, and wraps the featured apps (`data-slot="home-featured"`); below 768 px the chips and featured apps give way to it, so home is one screen. The site header shows the three-line menu at the top left on a phone (the kit's panel trigger from 768 px up) and no title on home there; `MobileTabBar` (Home, Apps, Library), rendered by `src/app/layout.tsx` after the inset, is a floating bar on every phone screen but the build screen. The sidebar's and header's active page is matched from the current path, not the router's settled location, which lagged a navigation, so after a click the header named the page before.
